"40,000 members and nobody does anything"

By lowob · 18 September 2026 · 5-minute read · Growth

A large, silent community was recruited for a payout and never given a job. Pick one job, recruit thirty people by name, ask for judgment, close the loop, and count who stays when the incentives stop.

What it usually means

The number is not the problem. The number is the symptom. When forty thousand people are present and nobody acts, three things are usually true at once.

They were recruited for a payout. An airdrop, a points programme, a giveaway, a quest. The incentive did its job and brought people in. It also selected for people who wanted the incentive. When it ended, their reason for being there ended with it. They did not leave. They just stopped.

They live on a rented platform. The record of who they are, what they said and what they did sits in a server or group you do not control. You can broadcast to them. You cannot really reach them, and you cannot take them with you.

The only shared interest is price or launch news. There is no problem being solved together, no product being tested, no decision being made. So the channel fills with questions about dates and goes quiet in between.

A community is a group of people doing a job together. This group was never given one.

Where it traces to

This traces to Part 5 and Part 6, with Part 18 for crypto teams.

Part 5 said community is a job, not a number. Five jobs: test, teach, refer, build, govern. If none of those was ever assigned, the community has nothing to do. Silence is the correct response to no job.

Part 6 said the first hundred are recruited by name, asked for judgment, given a job and shown what happened to their input. The forty thousand skipped the first hundred. The foundation was never laid.

Part 18 covered community that survives the airdrop. If a token or points programme was the recruiting tool, that part explains why the incentive produced a list rather than a group, and what to do about it.

The first move this week

Pick one job. Not five. One. The right one is whatever your product most needs this quarter. Early product means testing. Complex product means teaching. Working product means referring.

Hand-recruit thirty people by name. Go through the channel history and find the people who asked a real question, filed a bug, or helped someone else. Message each one directly. Tell them what the job is and why you picked them.

Ask them for judgment on a real decision. Not a poll. Not a sentiment check. A choice you have not made, where their answer changes what you do. Pricing, a feature cut, a launch order. Then make the decision.

Close the loop in public. Tell the wider channel what the thirty said, what you decided, and why. This is the moment a list starts becoming a community. People see that input leads somewhere.

Switch incentives off for a month. No points, no quests, no rewards for activity. Count who is still present at the end. That number is your real community. Build from it.

Move the record to channels you own. An email list, a members' directory, a database of who did what. The rented platform can stay as the venue. The record leaves.

What not to do

Do not buy more members. Adding people to a group with no job adds silence.

Do not run another quest campaign. It will produce a spike in activity and then exactly the same quiet, with a larger list.

Do not announce a token to wake it up. A token is an incentive. You have just learned what incentives recruit. It also creates a promise you will have to keep in public, under worse conditions.

How you know it worked

Two signs. First, the thirty are still active thirty days after the incentives stopped, and at least half of them have done the job without being asked twice. Second, one decision you made this month can be traced to their judgment, and the channel knows it.

The checklist

One job chosen, and thirty people recruited for it by name.

One real decision put to them, made, and reported back in public.

Incentives off for a month, retention counted, and the member record moved to a channel you own.

lowob takeaways

  • Members recruited by airdrops, points or quests stop acting when the incentive ends.
  • Hand-recruit thirty people who asked real questions, filed bugs or helped others, and message each directly.
  • Do not buy members, run another quest campaign, or announce a token to wake the group up.
